flashcards.definition: A counting unit equal to $$6.022\times10^{23}$$ representative particles, connecting atomic-scale quantities to measurable laboratory amounts.
The mass of one mole of a substance, usually expressed in grams per mole, and numerically equal to the substance’s formula mass.
The exact counting constant used to convert between particles and moles in chemical calculations.
An analytical technique that separates ions according to their mass-to-charge ratio, allowing determination of isotopic abundances and average atomic mass.
The weighted average of the isotopic masses of an element based on their natural abundances.

multipleChoice.questionText: A sample of an element contains two isotopes: one with mass $$10.01\ \text{amu}$$ and abundance $$19.9\%$$, and one with mass $$11.01\ \text{amu}$$ and abundance $$80.1\%$$. What is the average atomic mass of the element?
A chemist has $$0.250\ \text{mol}$$ of a compound. How many representative particles does the sample contain?

fillInTheBlank.questionText: The number of particles in $$1\ \text{mol}$$ of any substance is called ______.
In a mass spectrum, the x-axis typically represents ______.

flashcards.definition: The arrangement of electrons among atomic orbitals in a ground-state or excited-state atom or ion, following energy and filling rules.
The guideline that electrons occupy the lowest-energy available orbitals before higher-energy orbitals are filled.
The rule that electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing occurs.
A technique that measures the energy required to remove electrons from atoms or ions, revealing orbital energies and electron arrangements.
A predictable variation in a physical or chemical property across periods and down groups due to changes in effective nuclear charge, shielding, and distance from the nucleus.

multipleChoice.questionText: Which ground-state electron configuration is correct for sulfur, $$Z=16$$?
Which statement best explains why first ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period?
options: Effective nuclear charge increases while shielding changes only slightly.
Atomic radius increases dramatically across the period.
Valence electrons are added to a new principal energy level.
Nuclear charge decreases because protons are added less rapidly than electrons.
multipleChoice.correctAnswer: Effective nuclear charge increases while shielding changes only slightly.

fillInTheBlank.questionText: The experimental technique that determines electron binding energies by measuring emitted electrons after photon absorption is ______.
According to the ______ principle, electrons fill the lowest-energy orbitals available first.
